newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna bomber among Austria hostage takers. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Vienna bomber among Austria hostage takers. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]

text.p: A Palestinian convicted for his role in a 1985 (Corrects from 1987) bomb attack at Vienna airport and two other convicts took three prison staff hostage on Thursday, Austrian police said.

Two guards were injured, one of them seriously, during the incident in the southern Austrian town of Graz. Police said they were still negotiating with the hostage takers, who demanded a ransom and a getaway helicopter.

"The situation is very dangerous," a spokeswoman for Austria's interior ministry told Reuters. "The negotiations are still going on. The situation could change any minute and we are afraid for the hostages' lives."
The prisoners had strapped explosives to the bodies of the hostages and threatened to kill them if their demands were not met, Austrian news agency APA reported.

Police in Graz identified one of the men as Tawfik ben Ahmed Chaovali, 36, who was sentenced to life imprisonment for his role in the 1985 bombing which killed four people. The two other men were identified as Adolf Schandl, 60, and Peter Grossauer, 39.

Schandl gained notoriety in Austria when he forced his way out of an Austrian prison 25 years ago after taking one guard hostage. He was recaptured two weeks later. Grossauer was sentenced to 16 years in prison for a murder committed in 1989.
The interior ministry said it had dispatched specialist police forces trained to deal with hostage situations to the prison, which had been sealed off.
One of the guards was stabbed with a knife when he tried to prevent the hostage-taking. He and the other injured prison warder were taken to hospital by helicopter, police said.
